acceptance_criteria: AC-1 A run whose change state is `changed` carries a summary naming each section that gained, lost or altered entries, with its context and its old and new counts.
AC-2 A section present only in the new index is reported as added; one present only in the old is reported as removed; one in both with a different count is reported with both counts.
AC-3 Two index entries that differ only by source are treated as different entries, so a Palo Alto category whose provenance moved is not silently reported as unchanged.
AC-4 A first run and an unchanged run carry no summary.
AC-5 A predecessor with no stored index yields an explicit not-computable summary, never a list reporting every section as added.
AC-6 No configuration value appears anywhere in the summary, its persistence or its tests; a test asserts the summary contains only section names, contexts and integers.
AC-7 The named test suites pass with the new tests, and the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_14I_ARTEFACT_LOCATION_OPERATOR_RETRIEVAL_DEVIATION_AND_MANAGEMENT_SERVERS.md -- FROZEN, Product Owner directives 2026-09-14. DV-1: every artefact carries a plaintext digest and the product compares each new artefact with the previous one of the same class for the same device, recording unchanged, changed or first. DV-2: for the text-shaped artefacts -- Check Point Gaia configuration, Palo Alto running configuration -- `changed` is refined into a structural deviation summary: which sections gained, lost or altered entries, by section name and count, never by value; the Check Point section index and the Palo Alto category index already computed for the configuration view are the inputs, and nothing new is read from a device. DV-3: a Gaia system backup archive is opaque, so its deviation stays digest-level only and the product says so rather than implying it inspected the contents. DV-4: deviation is shown on the device's backup and configuration views.
baseline.engineering_baseline: The index is computed at collection time and stored with the run. The change state is already derived against the previous run in the worker's configuration executor, around line 144.
baseline.product_baseline: Configuration collection stores a run per device with its section index and a change state against the previous run. Nothing is read from a device by this movement; every input is already held.
baseline.test_baseline: The ui2 persistence, service and worker test suites pass on origin/main today.
baseline.what_exists:
A run is `record ConfigurationRun(String runId, String deviceId, String jobId, Instant collectedAt, String vendor, String readKind, boolean primary, String canonicalHash, String rawHash, long rawBytes, String artefactRef, int withheldLineCount, Optional<String> sanitizedText, String changeState, List<ConfigurationIndexEntry> index, List<ConfigurationOverride> overrides)`.

The index entry is `record ConfigurationIndexEntry(String context, String section, Optional<String> source, int entryCount)` -- one `device_configuration_index` row (13F CF-1, 14G CG-6): a section or category count within one context. Its `source` carries Palo Alto's per-element provenance (CG-7a: `tpl`/`dg`/`shared`/`local`) counted per category (CG-7b), and is empty for Check Point, which has no such attribute.

The change state is derived in ui2/worker/src/main/java/com/securityexpert/nexus/ui2/worker/configuration/ConfigurationJobExecutor.java, where line 144 reads `String changeState = previous.isEmpty() ? ChangeState.FIRST_RUN` and line 154 passes it into the run alongside `data.index()` and `data.overrides()`.

So both indexes -- the current run's and the previous run's -- are available at the point the change state is already being decided.

invariants: By section name and count, never by value. No configuration content leaves the parser.
Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence: a missing predecessor index is not an empty predecessor index.
Nothing new is read from a device; every input is already held.
The existing change state, digest comparison and override detection are unchanged.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Say what changed between two configuration reads, by section and count, never by value. Record 14I DV-2 requires that for the text-shaped artefacts a `changed` verdict is refined into a structural deviation summary: which sections gained, lost or altered entries. Today a run records only that it differs from its predecessor; an operator is told that something changed and nothing about where.
output_contract: An operator who is told a configuration changed can also be told which sections changed, and by how much, without ever being shown a value.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A comparison whose identity rule differs per vendor and whose central constraint is what must never appear in the output.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
The gradle commands run from ui2; the privacy gate runs from the repository root.
Every changed file names the clause it implements (14I DV-n).

If you add a migration, it is V22 and no other number, and if it writes to an audited table it sets app.actor_fingerprint and app.action_id transaction-locally -- read an existing audited migration and follow it exactly.
Run only the commands named above.
Run `git diff --check origin/main` before every commit and fix what it names.
Leave the worktree clean: write reports outside the repository or remove them before closing.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE states what identity you compared entries on, how a missing predecessor index is represented, and what proves no value can reach the summary.
risks: Comparing on section name alone, which collapses two Palo Alto categories that differ by provenance and reports a real move as no change.
Treating a missing predecessor index as empty, which reports an entire configuration as newly added the first time the index was stored.
Letting a value in through an example, a message, a log line or a test fixture -- the clause forbids values everywhere, not only in the persisted summary.
Computing the summary somewhere the previous run is not actually available, and reaching for the device or the artefact bytes to get it.

in: Compute, for a run whose change state is `changed`, a structural summary against the previous run's index: which sections appear only in the new index, which only in the old, and which appear in both with a different entry count. Carry the section name, the context it belongs to, and the counts -- old and new -- and nothing else.
Persist the summary with the run and expose it wherever the run's change state is already exposed, so a caller that can see `changed` can see where.

Respect the two vendors' shapes: a Check Point entry has no source, a Palo Alto entry has one, and two entries differing only in source are different entries. Compare on the whole identity the index actually has, not on the section name alone.

A run that is `first` or `unchanged` carries no summary, and an absent previous index is not an empty one: if the predecessor's index was never stored, say the summary could not be computed rather than reporting every section as added.
Tests: sections added, removed and recounted; the two vendor shapes; a first run; an unchanged run; a predecessor whose index is missing.
out: Any value from a configuration. Section names and counts only. Not a line, not a fragment, not a field value, not an example. This is the clause the movement exists to honour and it has no exceptions.
Any new read from a device, any new command, any new route to a device.
Any change to how the change state itself is decided, or to the digest comparison of DV-1.
Any treatment of the opaque backup archive. DV-3 keeps it digest-level and this movement does not touch it.
Any UI. DV-4's display is a separate movement.
Any change to the override detection that shares the same run.
